correctness.rationale: For any odd-order affine plane, the incidence matrix B satisfies BB^T=I+J over GF(2) and B^T 1=1; therefore B has all q^2 rows independent. Parallel-class line-column sums imply every row-codeword has identical parity on all q+1 classes; a word of weight at most two must be supported on two parallel lines, and the union of their point sets is its unique preimage. The left-kernel equation for one or two toggled entries proves the stated if-and-only-if rank loss of exactly one. Graph-state Schmidt entropy is this binary rank. The exact bad-pair count is (q+1)*C(q,2)*q^2 among C(q^2(q+1),2). All hypotheses, uniqueness, oddness, and edge-sharing cases are addressed. The complete q=3,5,7 finite test and q=9 field sample are corroboration, not replacements for proof.

value.rationale: The first damaging number of physically natural gate omissions is exactly two; among every placement of two faults on the geometry-based resource, their effect is classified by parallelism alone. This gives a complete and surprising all-order sharp defect threshold, an explicit rare-event risk q(q-1)/(q^2(q+1)-1), and a structural robustness criterion for an initially maximally entangled point-line register cut. Unlike a random numerical slice, the theorem covers every finite affine plane of odd order, including non-Desarguesian cases. It does not claim noise robustness or larger fault sets.
